lessons.title: How animals see and behave
lessons.html:
How animals see and behave

If you understand how animals think and see, you can move them calmly and safely. Calm animals are easier to work with, get fewer injuries and stay in better condition. Stressed or bruised animals lose weight and give poorer meat.

Herd animals

Cattle, sheep and goats are herd animals. They feel safe in a group and get upset when they are alone. A single animal that is cut off from the group may panic and jump fences or attack. Always move animals in groups where possible.

How animals see

  • Cattle and sheep can see almost all the way around them, but they have a blind spot directly behind them. If you stand there, they cannot see you and may kick or turn suddenly.
  • They do not see depth well. Shadows, puddles, bright light, a dark entrance or a change in floor colour can make them stop.
  • They move from dark to light more easily than from light into darkness.

The flight zone

Each animal has a personal space called the flight zone. When you step into it, the animal moves away. When you step back out, it stops. Tame animals have a small flight zone; wild or nervous animals have a big one.

The point of balance

The point of balance is at the animal's shoulder. If you stand behind the shoulder, the animal moves forward. If you stand in front of the shoulder, it moves backwards. By moving in and out of the flight zone and in front of or behind the point of balance, you can steer an animal without shouting or hitting.

Noise and smell

Animals hear very well. Shouting, whistling, barking dogs and banging gates scare them. They are also scared of strange smells, like blood in a race.

lessons.title: Moving animals in the veld and the kraal
lessons.html:
Moving animals in the veld and the kraal

Before you move animals

  • Know where the animals must go and the route.
  • Open the gates on the route and close gates that lead the wrong way.
  • Check the kraal, race and crush for broken rails, nails, wire and sharp edges.
  • Remove things that make animals stop, such as hanging coats, plastic bags, buckets in the race or a dog standing in the way.
  • Move animals in the cool part of the day.

Moving a herd in the veld

  1. Approach slowly and quietly from the side.
  2. Move into the edge of the flight zone so the herd starts walking.
  3. Walk in a zig-zag behind the herd to keep it moving at a walking pace.
  4. Do not rush. Animals that run get hot, bruised and injured, and may break fences.
  5. Let animals at the back catch up; watch for young, old or weak animals.

Working in the kraal, race and crush

  • Move small groups at a time; do not overfill the crowding pen.
  • Let the leaders move into the race; the others will follow.
  • Use flags, paddles or a plastic bag on a stick to guide. Never use sharp sticks or electric prodders on sensitive parts. Never twist tails or kick animals.
  • Close the head clamp in the crush gently and release animals calmly.

Sheep and goats

Sheep follow a leader. If one sheep goes through a gate, the others follow. Lead a quiet sheep through first. When catching a sheep, hold it under the jaw and at the back end; do not pull it by the wool, which bruises the meat. Goats are more independent and may jump, so fences must be higher.

Dogs and horses

Only well-trained herding dogs and riders should be used. A dog that bites or chases will make animals panic.

lessons.title: Loading, transport and safety
lessons.html:
Loading, transport and safety

Loading animals

  • Use a proper loading ramp with non-slip flooring and solid sides, at the right height for the truck.
  • Load calmly, in small groups. Do not crowd the animals.
  • Separate animals that may fight or hurt each other, such as bulls, horned and polled cattle, or big and small animals.
  • Do not overload the vehicle. Animals need space to stand and keep their balance.

Fit to travel

Do not load animals that are sick, injured, very weak or close to giving birth unless a vet says they may travel. Moving unfit animals causes suffering and can be an offence under the Animals Protection Act 71 of 1962.

On the road

  • Drive smoothly. Brake and turn slowly.
  • On long trips, plan rest stops with water.
  • Carry the documents the law and buyer require, such as proof of ownership and movement permits where disease control applies. The farm manager will arrange these.
  • Check the animals at stops.

Your safety

  • Never stand in the blind spot directly behind an animal.
  • Always know your escape route in a pen; never get trapped between an animal and a wall.
  • Be extra careful with bulls, rams, boars and mothers with young. Never enter a pen with a bull alone.
  • Do not climb into a crowded pen or a truck with loose animals.
  • Wear boots with steel toes where possible, and gloves.
  • Keep hands out of crush gates and head clamps when closing them.
  • Wash your hands after handling animals.

Key points

  • Animals feel safe in a group and get stressed when alone.
  • Use the flight zone and point of balance to move animals calmly.
  • Remove distractions from races and move animals slowly at a walk.
  • Never hit, kick or twist tails; use flags or paddles to guide.
  • Load only fit animals, do not overload, and drive smoothly.
  • Never stand behind an animal and always know your escape route.

quiz.question: Where is the blind spot of cattle?
Where should you stand to make an animal move forward?

options.text: Behind its point of balance at the shoulder
The area where birds fly over the kraal
An animal's personal space; when you enter it, the animal moves away

quiz.question: Cattle stop at the entrance to the race. What could be the cause?

options.text: A shadow, puddle or hanging object in the race

quiz.question: How should you catch and hold a sheep?

options.text: Under the jaw and at the back end

quiz.question: Animals that are moved fast and made to run can get bruised and lose condition.
A cow that is about to give birth may be loaded and transported without any special check.
What should you do before moving animals into the kraal? (select all that apply)

options.text: Remove plastic bags and other distractions
Bring a barking dog into the race
